W0501-R1-B-01.observed: The helper now compares whole digests and handles both shapes: normalizeDigest lower-cases, strips an optional sha256: prefix and returns the empty string unless the remainder is exactly 64 hex characters, and anyHashMatches compares EqualFold of the normalised values. The prefix-requiring bail-out and the want[7:24] slice are gone; the old call sites passed the truncated display list (installed entries built with sha(b)[:24]) and the new ones pass full digests. The data shapes are as claimed: main.go:74 returns 'sha256:'+hex while capabilities.json stores executor_sha256 = 8f0554ede25bbc5450921897c468b2e84635aa513c5017457997af0954581f49 as bare 64-hex, so the asymmetry the remediation describes is real.
W0501-R1-B-01.non_vacuity_measured: the control row requires control != '' AND anyHashMatches(digests, control) AND anyHashMatches(digests, 'sha256:'+control) AND NOT anyHashMatches(digests, pinned) AND len(normalizeDigest(pinned)) == 64. A helper that returns false for everything therefore fails the control (its first two conjuncts); a helper that returns true for everything fails both the control (the negated conjunct) and W0501-PINNED-EXECUTOR-IDENTITY-ABSENT-MEASURED. My matrix re-run produced exactly what the matrix file records: M16-executor-comparison-always-matches killed both PINNED rows with assertions_after 27; M17-executor-comparison-never-matches killed only the control with 28; M18-executor-pin-prefix-unnormalised (CutPrefix retargeted to sha512:) killed only the control with 28. Each of the three kills one of those rows by name, as the remediation claims.

W0501-R1-B-01.consequence: if the pinned build were reinstalled, both PINNED rows would go FAIL. Round 1's specific complaint (all rows keep printing PASS whatever the machine does) is closed.
W0501-R1-B-01.residual_limit: the control's positive half derives control from digests[0] itself, so it validates normalisation and equality rather than that sha() hashed the right bytes. That half is pinned elsewhere and I checked it: ARTIFACT-BOUNDED-TO-BYTES compares the adapter's own Hash() against the test's sha() over the same bytes, and the content_hash in my own run's journal (sha256:edd06c75ae0f62d744c17668402b708c4e0fce096e58052a4726ce4c72891831) equals the sha256 I recomputed from output.txt on disk.

blocking_issues.title: the new provider disclosure names the wrong blocked resource, pointing the remediation at the pinned executor binary when step 1 is blocked by an unbound client surface owned by other cards
blocking_issues.where: receipt.json check_results.not_verified row W0501-PROVIDER-MODELS-CONFIGURE-PROBE (source w0501.go:437-438) against execution/v2.4/client_mapping.json, internal/api/contracts/client.protocol.schema.json, internal/domain/client_protocol.go, execution/v2.4/commands.json rev 14 and execution/commands.json rev 5
blocking_issues.finding: the row says step 1's model directory, connection, authentication and real reasoning round trip 'are served by the provider model backend, which is blocked on this machine', and gives as its reason capabilities.json's unavailable model-tool entries plus the absent pinned executor binary, concluding that 'provider.models, provider.configure and provider.probe have no live counterpart to compare against'.
